utterances.text: One moment. I think the question referred to documents obtained from the Embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- here in The Hague, I would suppose.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think her question was Ministry of Interior and Embassy of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So I've answered Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What about the embassy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The Bosnian embassy has been forwarding us, I would say, documents which sometimes have been duplicates of what we have already received from Bihac and from other local offices in -- of AID offices in Bosnia. And again, let me point out that a lot of the material given to us by the liaison officers have been witness statements. They are of course documents that the BiH forces seized which have also been given to us, that is, copies of what we already got in Bihac earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: What I'm really interested in: Would it be possible that an organ of Bosnia-Herzegovina or a private person could give you a document which is not a witness statement without identifying the source of that document?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as witnesses are concerned, I don't think that is possible, because it is true witnesses have also given us documents, but the investigator who has taken possession of those documents is then duty-bound to ask for the source. So I don't believe that there are such cases where witnesses have given us documents where sources were not asked for. However, it is possible that the AID offices when investigators visit the field may have given documents and the investigators may have not checked about the sources of that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you do have documents in your offices the source of which is not known?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999, I know that many such documents where we did not have the sources, the staff from Office of the Prosecutor visited the field to authenticate those documents, that is, to compare the copies that we had with the originals that were being maintained in the field with the BiH authorities. And a lot of certification did take place. And personally I have reviewed in this exhibit list that I prepared that many documents have been certified in 1999 by our staff from the Office of the Prosecutor of the material that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, just dealing with that last point, when you say that the documents in the exhibit list were, as it were, certified in 1999, can you explain what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 1999, staff from the Office of the Prosecutor had identified key documents or, I would say, very important documents that were relevant to the ongoing investigations, and they took copies of those documents to Bihac where the -- all the seized collection is -- is being kept - excuse me - while in Bihac, staff of the Office of the Prosecutor then reviewed the copies we had and compared them with the originals that were being maintained in Bihac. After they had satisfied themselves that the copies we have are true copies of the originals, then the staff stamped those copies and signed those copies before bringing it back. So this is what I mean by "certification," or sometimes it is also referred as "authentication."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So that was a check to make sure that where we had only been provided with copies, the original was the same.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And let me just -- I beg to intervene and clarify something else, that this particular exercise had been also visually certified in 1995 and 1996. The person who received the copies in 1995 and 1996 had visually certified by looking at the copies, comparing those with the originals. So what happened in 1999 was to support that certification process one step ahead, you know, by stamping the material.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So in other words, you mean that the original investigator who had taken possession would have checked that the two appeared to -- or it wasn't a copy of the original document but hadn't stamped it to say that.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the only -- the question, actually, was to deal with the source. Are there documents -- what was put to you is there are documents in this institution of which the source, actually where the document comes from, is unknown. Now, are you able to reply about that -- a question like that?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: If those documents are mentioned in the disclosure list, then I can say with certainty that there is not a single document where the source is unknown. There may be just one, as I said yesterday, but I can look for the source of that document. But if her question was in a very general way, well, if it was -- is there any document in the whole Tribunal - I can't answer that - which has not been sourced properly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think, Ms. Korner, this was taken up yesterday when you were examining your witness. And if I remember well, and I think I do remember well, when we visited SU, being "source unknown," you said that documents falling under that category would no longer fall under that category because now the source had been established in the meantime. That's what you said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I didn't say it. The witness said it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There was a rather more general question put by Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But he has replied to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, those are all the questions I ask in relation to this exercise. Do Your Honours have any questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I personally don't. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you, then. If Mr. Inayat may step down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May I explain what I propose to do if this exercise is to be maintained. Of course there's still for Your Honours to make a ruling whether or not the documents which were the subject of objection should be admitted. But if these objections are going to be maintained, then I'm going to recall Mr. Inayat before we start the Banja Luka evidence to deal with the whole bundle of Banja Luka documents that we wish to put into evidence, going through exactly the same, if I can put it that way, rather tedious procedure and deal with the documents in those -- in that way. We will, however, this time pre-number the documents so that we don't have the confusion which was caused by me this morning. Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Inayat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may withdraw, thank you. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I have a suggestion that I think will eliminate or at least cut down dramatically this tedious procedure that we just went through. It seems to me that it is -- tends to be a waste of the Tribunal's time for Mr. Inayat to be called in here to say this document came from such and such a source.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If Ms. Korner would simply give us the information that she would elicit from him, that would dispose of perhaps most, if not all, of the foundation objections that we have. For instance, today's documents, if I had known before Mr. Inayat testified what he was going to say about many of these documents, I would have withdrawn my objections. It's clear that they did come from an official source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau, would you associate yourself with Mr. Ackerman in that practical suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, Your Honours, I support Mr. Ackerman's proposition.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact both Defence counsel are in possession of the indices which identify in each case the source, not to the same extent that Mr. Inayat has done today, in other words, that it was an investigator called Grant MacIntosh. But in the accompanying annex, one will see the legend which indicates every source. If what's required in each case is to identify which investigator from which person, then yes, certainly we can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take it that this is what you will be doing?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, if that's what's required, because the source, as I say, is already indicated on the index. So if I could just ask whether we're required to go into more depth, then we'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be more specific, the index that Ms. Korner is referring to, the presumed author is indicated and not the source of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't think anywhere in that index it says that these documents we were dealing with this morning came from Boro Blagojevic. I don't think that's there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's certainly correct. If that's the sort of information, we will do that exercise. Your Honour, that's very helpful, and I'm grateful to both counsel for that assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Chamber too is grateful. That's how actually we would like to see this trial proceed, with this spirit of cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, then the only matter remains for Your Honours to make a ruling before Mr. Donia comes back, whether the documents that were the subject of dispute should be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and I think we will need to suspend the sitting for a while in order to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the sitting is being suspended for half an hour, 30 minutes. We will resume at 12.30 sharp and we will come back with an oral decision, obviously. In the meantime, please do prepare Dr. Donia to start giving evidence because then we will not break as we would have done at half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. --- Break taken at 12.02 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good or bad news, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No news, Your Honour, which is, of course, always good news. Dr. Donia is here. He's getting used to his almost permanent stay now in The Hague. The only thing left to do is for you to rule on the documents and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Precisely what we are going to do, with the understanding that this is an oral decision which will remain an oral decision. It will be not -- it will not be reduced into writing, unlike the decision that we gave yesterday. This is an oral decision which this Trial Chamber is giving on the objections raised by the Defence teams of the two accused as to the admissibility of several documents on which Mr. Inayat gave evidence this morning. The Chamber's decision gathers together all these documents objected to in one basket because in its opinion what will be decided applies equally to each of these documents irrespective of the source of the objection. The Trial Chamber is of the opinion, the unanimous opinion, that on the basis of its oral decision of yesterday, January the 28th, relating to the various rules of admissibility of evidence that will be followed in the course of these proceedings, all the contested documents deserve to be admitted in evidence at this stage, particularly for the reasons that I will be mentioning. First, the testimony of Mr. Inayat attributes to each of these documents a source, which in the present circumstances this Trial Chamber has no reason to doubt, saving of course the eventual weight which will or will not be given to the same documents, depending on the evidence that will be forthcoming. Second, the terms in which the various objections raised by the Defence teams were conceived and presented are not such, in the opinion of the Trial Chamber, as to render the said documents a priori devoid of those indicia of reliability which the testimony of Mr. Inayat generally attributes to them. In the circumstances, therefore, the Trial Chamber is of the opinion and is actually disposing of the matter by authorising the admission in evidence of the documents in question. There is, however, a small number of documents that, as it transpired in the course of this morning's -- first part of this morning's hearing, have not yet been translated from B/C/S into the other languages of this Tribunal, particularly the English language. The Trial Chamber is deciding that their present admission will be reversed by this Trial Chamber if the translated version of these documents is not made available to the Defence and to this Trial Chamber within two weeks from today. I think we are giving ample time for this exercise. We're not talking of a large number of documents, and I think they can even -- on basing on the system which you proposed yesterday, they could be translated rather quickly. We are giving two weeks, in order not to put pressure on you. The registrar is also being directed hereby to give to all the documents exhibited this morning and admitted in evidence the official exhibit number. And that disposes of the matter. So I suppose we could now -- if you have nothing to add, we could now proceed by calling Dr. Donia, and he will resume his evidence from where he left it - he never really started it - but from where he left it on the first or the second day of this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just for absolute clarity -- your order is very clear, but just so that we know when you're referring to those documents, we're referring to the documents that are numbered Prosecutor's Exhibit 33 to 52, that those are admitted subject to the exceptions that you've mentioned in respect of translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. 3 to 52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The two volumes, the two binders, what was originally going to be and, I suppose, remains as the group of documents on which Dr. Donia will be examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the other document -- the other binder, which I suppose would serve the same purpose, the second binder is also documents on which Dr. Donia will be examined. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. So that is the position. I'm saying that the registrar must now proceed to give these documents their proper exhibit number, because a document does not really remain a document for the purposes of the trial. The moment it is admitted in evidence, it becomes an exhibit. And this is why I prefer, like other of my colleagues in other Trial Chambers, to use the same matter. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Your Honour, can we recall Dr. Donia, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please bring Dr. Donia in the courtroom. Now, Mr. Cayley, we need not wait for Dr. Donia, actually. But I would imagine that although Dr. Donia would have a copy of all these documents, they are probably not numbered the same reference -- exhibit numbers that we gave them this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: The witness has actually been following these proceedings, which he's allowed to do under the Rules, and he's actually numbered all of his documents basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What I propose to do, Your Honours, is if the Defence agree to this, is I will reference the tab number in the binder to identify where the document is in Your Honour's files and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And also --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: -- and I will also mention the exhibit number at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Agreed. We can proceed. Now, Dr. Donia, you will be handed -- will be given the same declaration that you were given the first time you came before this Trial Chamber, and you will be asked to make the usual solemn declaration. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may sit down. Now, Mr. Cayley from the Prosecution will continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, I'll just let you get settled. If you could have available your report. And I'd like to very briefly recap where we were last time in order to orientate everybody after these few days' break. And if you could go to page 42 of your report, which is the section on regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And what I would very briefly like you to do -- I don't want you to go over the general section on regionalisation, but I'd like you to very briefly summarise the section which begins "Regionalisation in Bosnian Krajina," which will take us right into the first series of documents which I'd like you to address.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April 1991, the SDS announced that it had begun a -- an effort to form a -- an association or a community of municipalities of the Bosnian Krajina, and I indicated that that began in January of 1991. On April 10th, 11th, and 12th, a number of municipalities with Serbian majority populations in which the SDS controlled an absolute majority of the municipal councils, assemblies, on those three days, a number of those municipalities declared their membership in the community or -- community or municipalities of Bosnian Krajina or the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Donia, if you could refer to the first document in your binder, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This, Mr. President, is a document that you will recall was, in fact, very kindly orally translated by the Defence on the last occasion that Dr. Donia was giving evidence. I don't think we need address the translation again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document reflects the decision of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc on the 10th of April, 1991 to join the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if you go to the next document, which appears behind Tab 1. And that's Prosecutor's Exhibit 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It might be helpful if the English version of this could be placed on the ELMO for the purposes of the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Whilst we're waiting for this, Dr. Donia - the Judges and the Defence have a copy of this document - could you explain what this document is, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the decision of the Municipal Assembly of Titov Drvar on 10 April 1991 to join the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We'll move to the next document, because they are all very similar. If you go to document behind tab 2, could you explain what that document is? That is Prosecutor's Exhibit 5.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the decision of the Bosanski Petrovac municipal assembly to withdraw from or separate from the socialist-era association of municipalities known as the Bihac Intermunicipal Regional Community.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm not going to go through all of these documents with you. If you could go to tab 5, the document behind tab 5, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 8, what is that document?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the decision of the municipal assembly of Laktasi to join the ZOBK on 11 April, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And the last in this series of documents, which is behind tab 6 and is Prosecutor's Exhibit 9, what is that document?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the decision of the Bosanska Gradiska municipality to join the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Donia, you've addressed five documents, and those documents, I think, are dated the 10th and 11th of April, 1991, the decisions of these various municipalities. What conclusions did you draw based on the examination of that series of documents, and in particular with reference to the dates?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the municipalities in question all voted to join the ZOBK within two days, and that led me to conclude that these decisions were a reflection of the SDS decision earlier in April to promote this ZOBK for Serbian-majority municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You've testified here before, Dr. Donia, but if you could try and pause between my question and your answer, that assists the interpreters, because they are also having to find these documents as well, as we go through. Now, in respect of these declarations, have you seen any other evidence that actually supports the fact that these decisions were made by these municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Banja Luka newspaper Glas, or Voice, followed these developments very closely and reported on a number of municipalities that voted to associate themselves with the ZOBK on the 10th, 11th and 12th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you recall from your memory any of the particular municipalities, the decisions of which we produced to the Court today, that were referred to in those newspaper reports, any single example?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall. I thought I had listed the municipalities in my paper but perhaps not. I do recall there was at least one municipality which was mentioned both in the newspaper and by decision of the municipal assembly as reflected in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I could direct you to page 45 of your report, do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Judges the reaction of other political parties in Bosnia to the creation of the ZOBK and these various declarations by municipalities in the Krajina region?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reaction in the first instance was considerable surprise. The leaders of the SDA criticised this development as a step taken by a single nation and one party, that is the Serbs and the SDS, and leaders of the other national party, the HDZ, similarly criticised the formation or these announcements as sudden and as having no basis in the relationship to the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Serbs, who were members of other parties, also reacted strongly. Milorad Dodik, the leader of the Reformist Party in the Bosnian Krajina, noted that his party was not a participant in this initiative, and said it was the act of a single party, the SDS, and suggested that it was required to work this out with the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. A spokesman for the Social Democratic Party expressed a similar concern that his party had learned of this only when the municipal assembly sessions were convened by their SDS presidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: How did the other political parties in the municipality of Kljuc react to the fact that the municipality had become a member of the ZOBK?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Kljuc municipality, representatives of two other parties, the SDA and MBO, two Muslim-dominated parties, stated that they had been misled into thinking that they were electing delegates to the old assembly -- or association of the Banja Luka municipalities and under that guise, they were brought into association with this yet to be formed ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What happened in Banja Luka at this time as a result of these declarations?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an effort in Banja Luka by the SDS leadership to vote in the municipal assembly for association with the ZOBK. However, the SDS did not have an absolute majority in that municipal assembly, which was large, it was 130 deputies. And in addition, one party member was opposed to forming ZOBK. Consequently, the SD -- or the municipal assembly of Banja Luka had not voted to join the ZOBK until very late in April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When you say "one party member," which party are you referring to? You said one party member objected.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: One member of the SDS objected.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: To joining the ZOBK?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What happened in Banja Luka on the 21st of April of 1991, as referred to in your report?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the 25th? No, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: On page 46 of your report you refer to a rally in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I'm sorry. The SDA, not content with these statements of surprise and opposition, organised a rally in Banja Luka, attended by some thousands of people, to protest the decision to move forward by these municipalities of the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And just to be clear, that was on the 21st of April?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the 21st, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Let's move ahead a little bit in time to the 25th of April of 1991, and if you can explain to the judges what was happening in the municipality of Celinac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. It should be okay now. You can proceed. Yes. Dr. Donia, I'm going to read out to you what you had just stated before the interpretation equipment registered a halt. You said, "Oh, yes. I am sorry. The SDA, not content with these statements of surprise and opposition, organised a rally in Banja Luka attended by some thousands of people to protest the decision to move forward by these municipalities of the ZOBK. And just to be clear, that was on the 21st of April? That was on the 21st, yes. Let's move ahead a little bit in time to the 25th of April of 1991. And if you can explain to the Judges what was happening in the municipality of Celinac." That was the question which Mr. Cayley put to you. And you had started replying to that question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll repeat that, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please, because that was missed completely by the interpreters, or the interpretation did not come through, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I just intervene on one matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, because the translation of the Glas article was essentially done by you, if you could read word for word that extract from your report into the transcript, rather than summarise it. That's on page 46.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: On April 25, 1991, the organising assembly, constituent assembly of the ZOBK was held in the municipality of Celinac. There were representatives of 21 municipalities present. 14 of those municipalities had already voted in their municipal assemblies to join the ZOBK. At that meeting, Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin welcomed the delegates on behalf of Celinac, the host municipality, and used the words in part: "We reject the Izetbegovic position of some state (structure) between federation and confederation. And if we go toward economic, cultural, and informational autonomy, we will seek people in this region who want to remain in Bosnia, but Bosnia remains in Yugoslavia. If (Izetbegovic) wavers on (supporting) the federation, we will waver on the Republic. We don't accept centralisation of economic and political power in Sarajevo." At that meeting, a president of the ZOBK was elected; that was Mr. Vojo Kupresanin. And two vice-presidents were selected from the remaining candidates; those were Mr. Brdjanin and Mr. Dragan Knezevic. In subsequent speeches, the president, the newly elected president, further asserted this theme of economic disadvantage in the Krajina imposed by Sarajevo and expressed solidarity with Serbs living in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, you stated earlier that 21 municipalities attended this meeting, 14 of whom had actually, I think -- you mention -- if you go to the bottom of page 46, you state: "21 municipalities attended, although only 14 municipalities had voted to join the association." And then you talk about the population distribution in those municipalities. If you can go to Table 1 in the body of your report, which is on page 48. Perhaps you can explain to the Judges exactly what you were getting at when you stated that.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I simply profiled the 1991 census results of the 14 municipalities that had voted by that time, by the 25th of April, to join the ZOBK. All except one of those - that was Kljuc - were municipalities with substantial Serbian majorities, well over 50 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you've already mentioned the part that comes next in your report, which is the Banja Luka situation in respect of joining the ZOBK. What I'd like to do now is to briefly address Table 2, which is the population -- the ethnic composition of those municipalities that were invited to join the Bosnian Krajina founding assembly. And at this time if you could say something about that for the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I simply looked at those municipalities that were mentioned at the -- in the press account of the meeting of the 25th of April and looked at the percentage of Serbs, Muslims, Croats, and Yugoslavs in each. It became evident that only one of those municipalities, that is -- or two, Banja Luka and Bosanski Novi, had absolute majorities of Serbs living in them. There were, I should add, other municipalities which were invited to join subsequent to the meeting of April 25th. And in fact at this time, let's say, the invitation to join was couched in voluntary terms, both in the language of the founding assembly and subsequently in the official newspaper of the SDS, Javnost.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that table of municipalities that you're referring to is on page 49 of your report, at the top.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Let's move on, Dr. Donia. If we can go to Tab 8 in the binder, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 11 and is the second session of the Bosnian Krajina Community of Municipalities. From this document, what were the initial concerns and decisions of that assembly?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The concerns addressed at the second meeting of the assembly, second regular session, centred on the adoption of a statute for the organisation and also on the establishment of certain institutions by the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you -- first of all, you mention the adoption of a statute for the organisation. Can you explain what happened in respect of that statute?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the first page of this document, which is P11, I believe, P11A in the English variant, there is a report on a discussion in which the president of the Banja Luka Municipal Assembly suggested that the draft statute should first be discussed by the municipal assemblies of the municipalities making up the ZOBK. This was -- the opposite position was taken by the vice-president, Mr. Brdjanin, who said, if I can perhaps cite it directly: "I propose that the statute be adopted today as it stands, because we cannot have a SZOBK" -- which would be an assembly of the ZOBK -- "on a voluntary basis. We cannot wait for public debate in the municipal assemblies and convene the community assembly every month." Subsequently, the Statute was passed unanimously by the ZOBK assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: In answer to an earlier question, you stated that this meeting also dealt with the establishment of certain institutions, and I'd like to direct you to item 3 within the extract of these minutes, where the proposals for the establishment of these institutions is discussed, and if you could please say a bit -- summarise what you stated in your report about the establishment of institutions?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That quote is on page 50 of the report and also the last several lines of item 3 in this document, which would be on the second page. These institutions already existed either at the level of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina or of federal Yugoslavia, and so this proposal to establish these institutions within the ZOBK constituted putting either new institutions or taking over the functions of existing institutions at the level of this new body.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Donia, the suggestion, amongst other things, is for the establishment of a ministry or secretariat of the interior, a judiciary, Prosecutor's Office, public auditing service, a university. Now, what is the significance of the ZOBK in recommending the establishment of these kinds of institutions?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were institutions that were characteristic of a separate state, a republic being formed, or some state-like entity being constructed. In the immediate post-socialist environment of 1991, these were all very important institutions in the -- particularly the economic and communications life of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can now move on in your report, still on page 50, to the next significant event which takes place, which is on the 27th of June of 1991, and it's subtitled "The Union of the Two Krajinas," can you explain to the Judges what happened during this time period?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of June, 1991, the leadership of the ZOBK launched a movement to unify with the Krajina across the border in Croatia. This consisted really of two separate acts, one of which was an agreement on cooperation and the other was a statement of political union. Just before this meeting, Nikola Koljevic, who was a member of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina and a leading member of the SDS, visited Banja Luka and cautiously warned that the central leadership of the SDS would not look favourably upon a statement of political union. Despite this, on the 27th of June, the assembly of the ZOBK held a joint meeting with the assembly of the Krajina across the border in Croatia. And at this meeting, they adopted both the declaration on cooperation and the proclamation of unity.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I could now direct you to the document behind tab 10 in your binder, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 13, and this is a stenogram or record of the session of the SDS, the central party of the SDS, which occurred on the 12th of July of 1991. My reason for showing you this document is to ask you the question: After the declaration on the union of the two Krajinas was made, how did the national SDS party react to this?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The national, that is the republic-level, leadership of the SDS, responded very critically to the proclamation of the union of the two Krajinas. Just perhaps to understand the context a bit, two days before this meeting, on the 25th of January -- or of June, 1991, Croatia and Slovenia, those assemblies of those two republics had issued statements of independence, and the -- I think that the members of the assemblies of the two Krajinas looked upon their declaration as closely related to those declarations of independence and justified on the basis of those withdrawals. The leadership of the republic-level SDS did not agree and criticised the formation or declaration as an unwarranted seizure of power and usurping the strategy, which had been adopted by the party at that time, of supporting federal Yugoslavia and its boundaries at the expense of challenges to those boundaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I could direct you to some extracts that you've identified within those minutes, first of all page 20, at the top, which is the minutes of what Dr. Radislav Vukic was saying during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The party was -- the SDS was at this point weighing a draft statute of its own, and Mr. Vukic, Dr. Vukic, on behalf of the ZOBK, said -- this is line 4 of that page 20: "On behalf of the regional board of Bosnian Krajina, I would, as regards the statute, call for more power, that is a greater chance for organisation, not only coordination of the regional board so that the people, deputies and assemblymen of Bosnian Krajina have greater democratic rights not to secede but to live together with the Serbian people, but to decide in the territory of the federal unit of Bosnian Krajina which will never let the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina," that is the Krajina across the border in Croatia, "fall into Ustasha jaws." This was a statement that, on behalf of the ZOBK, Dr. Vukic opposed, or he wanted included in the statute a recognition of the powers of the ZOBK. That was contrary to the draft statute that had been presented to the party as shown on page 23, when Mr. Trifko Komad is speaking, about two-thirds of the way down that page, where he's quoting from the draft statute. This begins with a dash and then three dots on that page, where he says, "That the main board shall decide on regionalisation and the regional organisation of the SDS." So in the draft statute as proposed by the party's leadership, this topic of regionalisation was to be assigned to the SDS Main Board. And on page 25, we have Mr. -- Dr. Karadzic responding to these two positions and essentially siding with those who had drafted the statute, where Dr. Radovan Karadzic begins to speak, the fourth line down, "Thus the idea of the re-regionalisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina has been present among the creators of SDS ideas from the very start, and the main board has always taken that into account. All ideas on regionalisation have originated from the main board." And then one line down, "I have to say one thing, we have to preserve the strength of the party not to give into power grabbing impulses and 'little Napoleons' who are trying to do things that will harm the Serbian people." On page 29, he goes on to address this question of the federal strategy, at the bottom of the page, the last full paragraph, "I have to say here that the policy of the Serbian Democratic Party is not to divide Bosnia and Herzegovina until others bring it to that point. The SDS furthermore does not approve of the creation of new federal units before the constitutional and legal system has broken down." He's referring here to the union of the -- very probably referring to the union of the two Krajinas. "This cannot be done under our aegis. Those who want to do things that are not in the platform and the statute of the SDS and the SDS views must form their own party."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So ultimately, at the republican level in the SDS, what was the view that carried the day in respect of the union of the two Krajinas?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The union of the two Krajinas in a sense perished from neglect. It was never mentioned, that I can find, in the official SDS paper, Javnost, and in fact, in early July, Dr. Karadzic used terms diametrically opposed to the union of the two Krajinas in referring to the Serbian nation having to defend the western border of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could move on now to the document which appears behind tab 13, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 16A - and this you deal with at page 52 and 53 of your report - can you explain to the Judges the significance of Prosecutor's Exhibit 16?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the notes -- documents that pertains to a meeting of the Assembly of the ZOBK and one of a number of references to the threatened situation of Serbs in the Krajina of -- across the border in Croatia. And in this document, the assembly in this communication states that "we will lead the people" -- let me identify that. Page 2, two-thirds of the way down the page, talking about the ZOBK itself. "Failing that, we shall lead the people to revolt and shall not be responsible for self-organisation." Then at the bottom of the page: "This decision also takes into account the order for the implementation of the final phase of preparations for the general mobilisation of the Territorial Defence and public security reserve forces, as well as the organisation of admission and arming of all volunteers in all municipalities of Bosanska Krajina." So this refers to another order which has been presumably issued which is not a part of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What is the date of this communication from the Assembly of the Bosnian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is 6 September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So from what you have just stated, you are presupposing that an order of some kind was made prior to the 6th of September to arm and establish volunteer units within the Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could now look at Tab 12, which is a document dated the 24th of August of 1991. This is Prosecutor's Exhibit 15, a document entitled "Command of Bosanska Krajina Volunteer Units." And if you could explain the significance of this document and link it with the prior document that we just referred to, Prosecutor's Exhibit 16.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this looks like the -- it is very likely the document referred to in the 6th of September meeting. This document consists of a cover sheet, signed by Colonel Ostoja Dejanovic, which begins -- this is on page 1 of this document: "We hereby enclose the essay submitted at the session of the representatives of the municipalities of Bosnian Krajina on the occasion of the establishment of the command of Bosanska Krajina volunteer units." The document that this refers to is then, I guess, four pages in English and makes numerous references to the relationship between this mobilisation of Territorial Defence forces and the JNA, the Yugoslav National Army. Just to indicate a few of those references, on what is the first English page of the attached document, page 22 is at the bottom, the second paragraph begins: "The JNA does not have enough forces to cover and protect all inhabited places." Then the fourth paragraph: "The volunteer units organised in this way have only one task to perform: to protect their people from being massacred by enemy forces which irrationally hate the Serbian nation. These units will never be sent to attack some other nation. Their role is purely defensive and nothing more. Volunteer units accept all tasks assigned to them by JNA units pertaining to the defence of the common state, peace, freedom, and equality of the nations which want to live in a common state and which they can carry out depending on their equipment and organisation." If I could just move to page 24, and the relationship of these volunteer units to the municipalities, the second paragraph there. It's the fourth, fifth, and sixth lines on page 24: "In order to facilitate better coordination, several municipal staffs should be linked in such a way that a single operative officer supervises several municipalities and coordinates their activities." So I think this document suggests a strong relationship between the ZOBK and a desire to organise volunteer units for defensive Serbian interests.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, before we leave that document, can I direct you to the final paragraph. And if you could just read that out for the benefit of everybody's attention.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 25: "The person who ordered ammunition depots to be opened and weapons to be distributed to the Serbian people obviously knew what he was doing. The Serbian people can now be sure that they have not been abandoned and that there are forces who are taking care of their safety."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, we have more or less five minutes left, so I don't know where you stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think I can get through one more document, Your Honour, before we finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I could take you back to Tab 9 of your report -- of the documents, I'm sorry, Tab 9 of the documents, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 12, and page 54 of your report. That's the relevant part of your report where you address this document. This is a document dated the 16th of September of 1991 and is an extract of the minutes of the seventh session of the ZOBK. What, if anything, is significant about the matters discussed in this particular minute?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision was reached at this -- excuse me. Let me pause here. The decision was reached at this assembly meeting to change the name of the ZOBK to letters that are easier to put together, the -- namely, the Autonomous Region of Krajina, or ARK. And in stating the nature of this decision, Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin said, and I'm quoting here from the first item, second paragraph: "By this decision, we are ensuring the region's independence. We do not want to bother anyone who does not want to leave Yugoslavia, but nobody here can be allowed to put various kinds of pressure on us, failure to construct major facilities, the oil shortage," et cetera. This decision was reached in the context of other regional associations being founded under SDS leadership in other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina with substantial Serbian populations. Those associations were called -- also called Serbian autonomous regions. There is a difference in the Serbian version of this between "regija," which is what the ARK was called, and "oblast," which also means "region" in English, but which is the title that the other autonomous regions were accorded by the central party leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And I think those -- the creation of those other autonomous regions are referred to in minutes of the main SDS and in another document. This, actually, would be a good place to stop, because I think tomorrow we can link those two documents together.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So Mr. President, if you're agreed, this would be an appropriate time to pause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have just a quick announcement here. Tomorrow we will be sitting in Courtroom III instead of Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The same time, 9.00, but in Courtroom III. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not quite certain how much additional time Mr. Cayley has to take, but with regard to preparation for cross-examination of Mr. Donia, I have been interrupted a bit but I've been working quite hard getting through all the documents. I think -- in fact, I will commit to the Court that I will be prepared to proceed Thursday morning at 9.00, if that's okay with everybody concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I anticipate, Your Honour, that my examination-in-chief may bleed over into Thursday. I'll move as quickly as I can through these documents, but you can see to do it sort of methodically and slowly is better than rushing them through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In any case, if that will happen, Mr. Ackerman and his client will certainly not suffer any prejudice. If anything, they will have more time. So that wouldn't create any problems. And the Defence for General Talic more or less should liaise with Mr. Ackerman. Mr. Ackerman should be in a position to tell you how long he expects to have his cross-examination last, and then you should be prepared, and you will be expected to be prepared to start immediately afterwards. Okay? Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If you want, just a little kind of small housekeeping matter that will have to be dealt with at some point. It seems to make sense that with regard to the order of cross-examination, what we did in Celebici, which worked extremely well, was we would announce to the Court at some point prior to the cross which counsel would go first because some witnesses are relatively unimportant to me and very important to the other side and so forth. And so if we just tell you in advance, we would hope that will work with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it definitely will. And it will be something that we would appreciate.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: One last point, Your Honour, that my learned friend Ms. Korner has raised with me is originally Dr. Donia had planned to leave on Saturday. He has other engagements, and obviously we hadn't anticipated the delays caused by procedural matters, and it would be helpful if the Defence at some stage - I realise not now until I finish my examination-in-chief - could give some kind of estimate of time for their cross-examination so that we can change things like airline tickets, extend hotel reservations. That would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I really don't want Dr. Donia to be required to stay in this place, where the wind blows 50 miles an hour constantly, any longer than he absolutely has to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's better than it was in some places in the United Kingdom and in Scotland yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Better than it is in Texas sometimes too. In any event, it would surprise me if we are not finished with Dr. Donia by Friday when we close our work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's as far as your cross-examination is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah. I really don't know how long the French will take, but -- I think that both of us can be finished by Friday afternoon, but I can't make that commitment because I don't know -- you never know in cross-examination what kind of responses you're going to get and what they lead to, and what I think will take two hours could take three so -- but the best I can do is that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, but I was waiting for the interpretation. I think that my cross-examination will not take very long. Obviously, it will depend on Mr. Ackerman's cross-examination, but a priori I think it will be between one and two hours on the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's very helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you can work on that basis and if that is what will actually happen, I mean, I think Dr. Donia can be on his way on Saturday. So we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. We will now go and finish the decision on Rule 92 and hopefully you should get it within the next hour or so. Thank you. See you tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.47 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 30th day of January, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
